summary: Off-registry HTTP dependency URL delivers arbitrary code at install time
details: package.json declares a dependency `aws-blog` whose source is the plain URL `https://repo.securityctrl.com/aws-blog` rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever bytes that URL returns and executes any lifecycle scripts contained within them, with no version pin and no integrity check. The dependency key matches this package's own name (dependency-confusion shape) and the version `45.0.2` is high enough to win resolution against an internal `aws-blog` package. The shipped index.js is an inert `hello()` stub, so the manifest URL is the sole delivery mechanism and the host `repo.securityctrl.com` is unrelated to any AWS or npm publisher domain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
